profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility is located at 1059 Forge Avenue, Lower Providence Township, PA 19403, in Montgomery County; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

PECO, the utility serving this Montgomery County facility, proposed rate hikes in April 2026 of 12.5% for electric and 11.4% for gas, effective 2027, on top of an already-taken roughly 10% increase earlier in the year; a coalition of Montgomery County lawmakers submitted a formal letter to the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission opposing the hikes, and state Sen. Katie Muth linked the increases directly to data-center-driven grid investment. Separately, the PUC finalized new guidelines in May 2026 requiring PECO's data center customers to sign transmission-security agreements including a 10-year letter of credit PECO can draw on if a promised data center is not built or under-uses its contracted power, a mechanism PECO began applying to planned sites elsewhere in its territory in late 2025.

Montgomery County's data center presence is smaller and more diffuse than the wholesale campuses clustered in Loudoun County, Virginia or Hillsboro, Oregon, reflecting its role as a secondary Philadelphia-suburb interconnection point rather than a hyperscale hub.

reading.body:
Lumen Norristown is a colocation facility in Lower Providence Township, Pennsylvania, owned by Lumen Technologies. No power capacity is published for this campus. Without a published figure, the campus cannot be ranked by capacity or compared to the state's other data center infrastructure.

Pennsylvania has 14 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 publish power capacity, totaling 22.2 megawatts. Lumen Norristown is ranked fifth in the state by published megawatts, but this ranking reflects only the four facilities with disclosed capacity; the ranking position has no meaning when the facility's own capacity is unknown.

Lumen's current colocation product pages claim 200 plus locations in North America and 120 plus cities, but no dedicated market or facility page for Norristown was found. Whether this facility is part of Lumen's retained colocation infrastructure or among the data centers Lumen divested to Cyxtera Technologies in 2017 is not published and could not be determined from available sources.
